Matplotlib's defaults are designed for quick interactive exploration, not for figures in a thesis
or journal article. A few deliberate choices (figure size matched to the final column width, labelled
axes with units, readable font sizes, distinguishable line styles) make a large difference.

The code below runs every time this page's source changes, and @fig-example shows its actual output.

```{python}
#| label: fig-example
#| fig-cap: "Decay of a sinusoidal signal, with axis labels, units and a legend."
#| echo: true

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t = np.linspace(0, 10, 500)
tau = 3.0

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(t, np.exp(-t / tau) * np.cos(2 * np.pi * t), label="signal")
ax.plot(t, np.exp(-t / tau), "--", color="0.4", label=r"envelope $e^{-t/\tau}$")
ax.set_xlabel("Time, $t$ (s)")
ax.set_ylabel("Amplitude (-)")
ax.set_xlim(t[0], t[-1])
ax.legend(frameon=False)
plt.show()
```
